The aim is to find and make explicit the overlap between user needs and business or profit, not to abandon user-centeredness.

sections.heading: Focus on the work with the most value
sections.content: Use research insights precisely—“like a scalpel”—and learn with partners to say no to lower-priority work. Antin describes researchers stretched across many projects as unlikely to do a good job; he advises researchers to focus on the most important work. He also urges them to understand where research can create the most value and push back when research is not contributing.

sections.heading: Build influence through partnership and integration
sections.content: Develop strong relationships through two-way engagement; researchers cannot create those relationships alone. Antin recommends being an excellent communicator and becoming more influential. He also recommends an integrated, lean product process in which researchers are involved from the beginning, and PMs help prioritize and partner with researchers. These relationships and early involvement can help research insights have greater impact.

answer.summary: Antin recommends researchers broaden their methods, understand the business, and build close partnerships so they can focus on high-value questions and contribute throughout product development.

sections.heading: Broaden your skills and business fluency
sections.content: Develop diverse, multi-method research skills: formative or generative research, evaluative usability work, rigorous survey design, applied statistics, and technical skills such as SQL or, increasingly, prompt engineering. Go deep on business knowledge too: learn the language of product, metrics, and business, and connect insights explicitly to where user needs and business outcomes overlap. Antin suggests learning about the business by reading a public company’s quarterly report or listening to its shareholder call.

sections.heading: Focus on the work with the most value
sections.content: Use insights precisely, understand which questions can have the greatest impact, and work with partners to prioritize and say no. Antin warns that researchers overloaded with many projects cannot do them all well; he describes a full plate as about three projects—two large and one small—as a rule of thumb, not a guarantee. He also recommends pushing back on research that will not contribute meaningfully.

sections.heading: Build relationships and integrate research into product work
sections.content: Create strong, two-way relationships with product partners, and make research part of the process from beginning to end—not a reactive service brought in at the end. Early, consistent involvement lets researchers help frame the right questions and bring insights into decisions. Antin also calls for researchers to become more influential and excellent communicators; companies and partners must help create the conditions for this impact.
